options.tooltip: Source video to edit or restyle (v2v, rv2v). Resized to width/height and trimmed to length.
Video to insert into the source video (ads2v).
Max size for the long edge of reference_video and reference_images. Resized with preserved aspect ratio and snapped to 16px.
Prompt elements from the node Create Bounding Boxes.
Optional description of the image in one or two sentences. Strongly recommended.
Mandatory description of the image background or environment.
Mandatory aesthetic keywords (e.g. moody, cinematic, desaturated).
Mandatory lighting description (e.g. golden hour, rim light, dramatic shadows).
Mandatory medium type (e.g. photograph, illustration, 3d_render, painting, graphic_design). When style = photo, set to photograph.

If true, rescale the combined noise BEFORE the sampler's CFG combine, without clamping (can amplify). Matches the norm-scaled CFG used by models like Lens. Default false keeps the original post-CFG x0-space attenuate-only behavior.
The text to be encoded.
The CLIP model used for encoding the text.
Azimuth around the subject in degrees. 0 is the front, 90 the right side, 180 the back.
Elevation in degrees. Negative looks up from below, positive looks down from above.
Lens zoom on the subject: 0 is a wide shot, 10 a close-up. Carried into camera_info.zoom.
Optional reference image shown on the front of the subject cube in the 3D preview.
The name of the checkpoint (model) to load.
When enabled, will delegate to an existing model function wrapper if it exists. Generally should be left enabled.
First sigma that these options will be in effect.
Last sigma that these options will be in effect.
Allows overriding the default NeRF tile size. -1 means use the default (32). 0 means use non-tiling mode (may require a lot of VRAM).

Force usage of sequential text token IDs instead of zeroes. Should be used for checkpoints from 2026-05-22 to 2026-06-01 that are trained in this way but do not contain the __sequential__ key in the state dict.
Spaces per indent level. 0 produces compact single-line string.
Spaces per indent level. 0 produces compact single-line string.
Optional image used as background in the canvas and preview.

Bounding boxes, elements, or a JSON string to initialize the canvas. A new upstream value initializes the canvas; edits made on the canvas take priority and are kept until the upstream value changes again.
Width of the canvas and the pixel grid for the bounding boxes.
Height of the canvas and the pixel grid for the bounding boxes.
Internal state managed by the canvas: the upstream bboxes value that last initialized it. Leave empty to re-initialize the canvas from the bboxes input on the next run.

Resolution the model runs at (longest side, multiple of 14).
Lower = faster / less VRAM.
Higher = more detail.
Output is upsampled back to the original size.

upper_bound_resize: scale so the longest side = resolution (caps memory, default).
lower_bound_resize: scale so the shortest side = resolution (preserves more detail on tall/wide images, uses more memory).

mono: single view image (works with any model variant).
multiview: all images processed together for geometric consistency + camera pose (for Small/Base models only).

- depth: normalised greyscale depth image.
- depth_colored: depth mapped through the Turbo colormap.
- sky_mask: sky probability in [0, 1] (for Mono/Metric models only).
- confidence: normalised depth confidence (for Small/Base models only).
Model used for the positive (conditional) pass.
Model used for the negative (unconditional) pass. Use the same model for ordinary CFG.
Negative conditioning run on the negative model. Leave unconnected for a text-free (image-only) unconditional pass.
The width of the latent images in pixels.
The height of the latent images in pixels.
The number of latent images in the batch.
The prompt text. Cite box N as <obj_N> to tie words to it.
Prompt elements from the node Create Bounding Boxes. Colour palettes are not used, describe colours in the description.
The model to use KV Cache on.
GLSL fragment shader source code (GLSL ES 3.00 / WebGL 2.0 compatible)
Output size: 'from_input' uses first input image dimensions, 'custom' allows manual size
Sampling progress (0=start, 1=end) at which the blend turns ON.
Sampling progress at which the blend turns OFF.
Shift layout. single_shift: one pass at the natural patch grid + others offset. symmetric: all passes off-grid, shifts split around origin.
Number of passes per gated step. 2/4 = fixed. ramp_*: pass count increases as sampling approaches end (more smoothing where seams are most visible).
average: equal-weight mean. window: Hann-windowed weighting favoring each pass away from its patch boundaries. median: per-pixel median, rejects wraparound-outlier passes.
Interpolation between the natural-grid pred (0) and the averaged result (1).
Reference images are used in numeric socket order.
Add a noise mask to the latent so sampling will only happen within the mask. Might improve results or completely break things depending on the model.
The model used for denoising the input latent.
The random seed used for creating the noise.
The number of steps used in the denoising process.

The Classifier-Free Guidance scale balances creativity and adherence to the prompt. Higher values result in images more closely matching the prompt however too high values will negatively impact quality.
The algorithm used when sampling, this can affect the quality, speed, and style of the generated output.
The scheduler controls how noise is gradually removed to form the image.
The conditioning describing the attributes you want to include in the image.
The conditioning describing the attributes you want to exclude from the image.
The latent image to denoise.
The amount of denoising applied, lower values will maintain the structure of the initial image allowing for image to image sampling.
The model used to remove backgrounds from images
One flat color per region, at the output size. The colors are only region IDs.
Depth map at the output size, near is white.
Scales the maps' contribution to the image tokens. 0.0 is the same as no maps, 1.0 is the trained strength.
Sampling percent at which the control starts.
Sampling percent at which the control ends. Ending early keeps the layout and depth while the rest of the steps loosen the shapes.
Description of the whole image.
Prompt elements from the node Create Bounding Boxes. The description is the box's caption, text boxes also render their text.
Width of the generated image; the boxes are placed in its pixels.
Height of the generated image; the boxes are placed in its pixels.
Numbers of the object boxes to label as characters instead of objects, as tagged in the Create Bounding Boxes preview, e.g. "1, 3".
The MiniMax-H3-Image VAE. With it the pictures are also anchored as reference latents, without it they only condition the text encoder.
0 uses the width of image_1 after its reference scaling, or 2048 without images. The model is tuned for 2048x2048 pixels of area
0 uses the height of image_1 after its reference scaling, or 2048 without images.
0 = fastest, 9 = most detail.
Horizontal field of view of the source camera. Sets the focal length used to unproject the depth map into 3D. 0 = auto-recover from the predicted points.
Images per inference call. Lower if you OOM on a long video / image set.
Set masked-out (sky / invalid) pixels to inf in points and depth so meshing culls them. Disable to keep the raw predicted geometry everywhere; the mask is still returned separately.
MoGe-3 only: sparse volumetric refinement passes over the predicted depth. More passes sharpen fine detail and edges at a roughly linear cost. 0 disables refinement. Ignored by MoGe-1 / MoGe-2.
DirectX vs OpenGL controls the normal-map green-channel convention. DirectX: green = -Y down (Unreal). OpenGL: green = +Y up (Blender, Substance, Unity, glTF).
Absolute training noise scale. For example HiDream-O1 base: 8.0, dev: 7.5.
The p-h3-image VAE. With it the pictures are also anchored as reference latents, without it they only condition the text encoder.
With images a short instruction gets "Edit <Picture 1>. " in front; an instruction that starts with "Edit <Picture" and an edit brief from the prompt upsampler are used as they are.
0 uses the width of image_1 after scaling, or 2912 without images.
0 uses the height of image_1 after scaling, or 2912 without images.
Optional base image to paint over
latent (from VAEEncode or a KSampler).
Flux1 (16-ch) and Flux2 (128-ch) latents are auto-detected from channel dim under 'flux'. For SD3 (16-ch), SDXL (4-ch), or QwenImage (16-ch), select manually.
0 = clean latent. Increase to denoise corrupted latent outputs.
auto uses spare VRAM, then RAM. cpu (RAM) is prefetched behind compute and costs little speed. off recomputes the prefix every step, which is slower but is the one way to rule the cache out.
Storage precision. default is lossless. int8 halves the cache at about bf16 accuracy, int4 quarters it but roughly doubles the per-step error.
Filter detections by class. Set to 'all' to disable filtering.
Maximum number of detections to return per image. In order of descending confidence score.
Reference images are ignored when no VAE is connected.
When enabled, the dot (.) character will match any character including newline characters. When disabled, dots won't match newlines.
Maximum number of replacements to make. Set to 0 to replace all occurrences (default). Set to 1 to replace only the first match, 2 for the first two matches, etc.
Background removal model used to generate the mask
Input image to remove the background from
Select how to resize: by exact dimensions, scale factor, matching another image, etc.
Interpolation algorithm. 'area' is best for downscaling, 'lanczos' for upscaling, 'nearest-exact' for pixel art.
The aspect ratio for the output dimensions.
Target total megapixels. 1.0 MP ≈ 1024x1024 for square.
Live preview of the calculated output resolution.
Nearest multiple of the result to set the selected resolution to.
Text conditioning from CLIPTextEncode
Bounding boxes to segment within
Positive point prompts as JSON [{"x": int, "y": int}, ...] (pixel coords)
Negative point prompts as JSON [{"x": int, "y": int}, ...] (pixel coords)
SAM decoder refinement passes (0=use raw detector masks)
Output per-object masks instead of union
Optional bounding boxes for more accurate detections. Required for multi-person detection.

Stochastic strength of SDEs.
When eta=0, they reduce to deterministic ODE.
Large eta may cause invalid outputs. If this occurs, try decreasing this value.
Per-step noise multiplier at the first step (1.0 = match training).
Per-step noise multiplier at the last step. Set equal to s_noise for a constant schedule.
Clamp per-step noise to +/- N*std. 0 disables.
The images to save.
The prefix for the file to save. This may include formatting information such as %date:yyyy-MM-dd% or %Empty Latent Image.width% to include values from nodes.
The images to save.
The prefix for the file to save. May include formatting tokens such as %date:yyyy-MM-dd% or %Empty Latent Image.width%.
The file format in which to save the image.
The SeedVR2 model.
The generated image to process.
The original resized image before pre-processing, used as reference.

Method to match the generated image colors to the original image. lab: transfer color in CIELAB space, preserving detail (most faithful). wavelet: transfer low-frequency color, keeping upscaled high-frequency detail. adain: match per-channel mean/std (fastest, global tint). none: skip color transfer (geometry alignment only).
The resized image to process.

Controls the rescaling strength.
Lower k produces more detailed results; higher k produces smoother results in image generation. Setting k = 1 disables rescaling.

Controls how early rescaling takes effect.
Larger values take effect earlier.
Reference image(s) to edit. Boogu focuses on one reference per sample; more are allowed.
Empty is the null caption Fibo 2.0 was trained with for CFG with edit workflows.

Images to edit, referred to as <image_1>, <image_2> and so on in the instruction. A single image is scaled and center cropped to the result's size, since the edit lines up with it pixel for pixel; several images each to their own trained size.
Width of the result. 0 = the size Fibo 2.0 was trained at for the first image's aspect ratio, about 1 megapixel, or 1024 without images.
Height of the result. 0 = the size Fibo 2.0 was trained at for the first image's aspect ratio, about 1 megapixel, or 1024 without images.
Encodes the images as reference latents for the edit LoRA.

The layout the edit LoRA was trained with: ai-toolkit's MOSS-Image Edit Training (its kv_cache option on or off) or Moss-Image-Edit. With kv_cache off the references also attend to the image being generated, so they are recomputed every step.
Scales how much the model attends to the images the text encoder sees (ai-toolkit formats, or no VAE): 0 ignores them, 1 is unchanged, above 1 emphasizes them.
Reference image(s) to edit. All references are resized to the output resolution before encoding.
Output width. 0 = use the first reference image's size.
Output height. 0 = use the first reference image's size.
Without a VAE the images only condition the text encoder through the vision tower.
Optional reference images, seen by the text encoder and appended to the latent sequence as clean frames. Later images are resized to the first one, and the sampled latent should match its size.
Reference images are resized to about resolution x resolution pixels, at multiples of 32, preserving aspect ratio. 0 keeps each reference at its own size, rounded to a multiple of 32.
Reference images, seen by the text encoder and spliced into the sequence as VAE latents.
Operate in thinking mode if the model supports it.
Use the built in system prompt/template if the model has one.

Speculative decoding with the checkpoint's multi-token-prediction head. No effect without MTP weights. auto adapts the draft depth and breadth to observed token matches and execution cost; 2-5 pins a constant draft depth; tree modes pin both breadth and depth. Sampled output stays correctly distributed but differs from non-MTP output for the same seed.
Replaces the system prompt in the model's chat template. Ignored when the default template is not used.
The latent to be decoded.
The VAE model used for decoding the latent.
Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to decode at a time.
Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to overlap.
Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to encode at a time.
Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to overlap.
Fills the padding frames of the image conditioning with this image instead of gray, anchoring identity without pinning frames (SVI-style anti-drift padding, used by models such as ID-V2V).
